long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Alexandria to a schoolteacher, Mohamed Al-Fayed began as a salesman before working in Saudi Arabia. He later built shipping and construction connections across the Gulf. After moving to Britain, he assembled a portfolio of prestige businesses, acquiring the Ritz Paris, House of Fraser and its Harrods flagship. The eventual Harrods sale crystallised the largest part of his retail-and-investments fortune.

Al-Fayed bought Fulham Football Club in 1997 and funded its climb from England's third tier to the Premier League and a European final. He later sold the club, remained an Egyptian citizen despite long campaigns for British nationality, and died in 2023. After his death, many women reported sexual abuse. The Metropolitan Police later described a continuing inquiry into people suspected of facilitating his offending, while noting that he could no longer face prosecution.

uncertainties.detail: Identity is resolved at 100 without private-asset facts. The exact name, Egyptian nationality, United Kingdom residence, age, Harrods image and business chronology converge with Forbes, Companies House, Fulham and family-confirmed death reporting for the same businessman.

The British trade inquiry, AP and the Guardian support 27 January 1929, which also fits the family-confirmed age of 94 at death. Companies House and the source record reflect the 1933 year Al-Fayed publicly used. The dossier proposes the investigated 1929 date at high rather than very-high confidence and preserves the conflict explicitly.

The stored Alive status is demonstrably stale and is proposed for correction to Deceased. Because the immutable inventory treats death fields as inapplicable while that status remains Alive, 30 August 2023 and age 94 are retained as dependent candidates for review after the mortality correction rather than direct proposals.

Hospitality reflects the Ritz Paris as the principal flagship business that remained after Al-Fayed sold Harrods and Fulham. Retail was the historically defining wealth engine, and Diversified is used independently for wealth creation because the fortune also involved shipping, Gulf contracts, property and sports.

Forbes labels Al-Fayed self-made, but his Saudi employment, marriage into the Khashoggi family and later Gulf relationships supplied meaningful commercial access. Self-made — advantaged start recognises that access without treating it as an inherited operating fortune. Public reporting and the trade inquiry also dispute parts of his own origin story.

Numerous people have reported sexual abuse by Al-Fayed, but his death prevents a criminal prosecution of him. The long biography attributes the reports and uses the Metropolitan Police's March 2026 description of an active investigation into suspected facilitators; it does not state that a court convicted Al-Fayed or that current suspects are guilty.

The dedicated Forbes profile clears exact-person verification. No personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website with defensible control by Al-Fayed was found, and no deceased-person fan or memorial account is proposed.

Department stores, Hotel operations and Football are active catalogue concepts and each captures a sustained, defining ownership or operating mandate. Inactive narrower terms such as Football club owner and Hotel operator are excluded, while Luxury goods is omitted as redundant with the more specific Department stores tag.

All private-vessel names, relationships, specifications, values, movements and holding structures are excluded from both biographies and every wealth determination. The dossier also avoids current net-worth figures, disputed transaction-price detail and private family or residence material.
